QuickAdd.dc.html.title: Quick add to My Day — Ctrl+Alt+Space

futuretitle.text: Future features — each note stands on its own

ff1.text:
Project progress bars

Top-level project rows show a thin progress bar and done/total (e.g. 4/13) right after the title. Counts every descendant; cancelled tasks are left out of both numbers. Collapsed parents already show done/total, so this only adds the always-visible bar on projects.

From: variant A.

ff2.text:
Now card in My Day

When a task is Doing, it gets a pinned card at the top of My Day with its path, title and three actions: Done (Space), Worked on (W), Pause (S). The rest of My Day lists below as Next, and finished items fold into a single “Done today · n” line.

Decide first: can more than one task be Doing at once?

From: variant A.

ff3.text:
Zoom into a task (Logseq-style)

Ctrl+→, or clicking a task’s bullet, narrows the tree to that task and its subtasks, with a breadcrumb on top (All › Fridge 3 › Milestone 2). Ctrl+← or Esc steps back out one level. New tasks, indenting and dragging stay inside the zoomed scope. My Day and the day column are unaffected. Remember the zoom across restarts.

ff4.text:
Project sidebar

A left rail listing My Day, Inbox and each top-level project with its open-task count and a progress bar; Ctrl+1…9 jumps between them. Choosing a project zooms the tree into it (builds on the zoom feature). Add only once the tree gets too long to manage by collapsing.

From: variant B.

ff5.text:
One-outliner layout

An alternative layout with a single outline column: My Day is its first section (numbered, in order), then Inbox, then Projects. T pins a row into the top section; dragging between sections works as in the tree. Could ship as a layout setting, useful when the window is snapped to half the screen.

From: variant C.

ff6.text:
Day filter rail

A small panel listing Overdue, Today, each weekday, Next week, Later and No day, each with a count bar in the day-column colours. Clicking one filters the tree to tasks on that day; clicking again clears it. Works with either layout, and pairs well with the one-outliner layout.

From: variant C.

designnotes.text:
Notes on the design

• Layout: tree 60% / My Day 40%. Task detail opens in place of My Day (Esc returns).
• Rows are 26 px in the tree and 44 px in My Day, where each item carries its grey path.
• Statuses: open, doing (blue box + filled square), worked on (half orange circle), done (tick), cancelled (× in checkbox, struck through, left out of the day's count).
• Day column on the left of the tree: red = overdue, blue = today, fading to grey at two weeks out.
• Scheduling: D on any task (or Pick a day… in detail) opens the day picker: 1–9 = today … 8 days out, arrows + Enter in the calendar, dots show how full a day is. The morning review uses the same picker.
• Adding to My Day: T on a selected task, N in My Day, Ctrl+Alt+Space from anywhere.
• Morning review: one running list. A S D F = Today / Another day / Backlog / Drop; Z undoes. Sorted rows are tinted by outcome: blue today, purple another day, grey backlog, red dropped.

Open questions
1. Does “Drop” delete the task or mark it won't-do?
2. Can more than one task be Doing at once?
3. When a parent is scheduled today, do its children appear in My Day too?
4. Name ideas: Daybook, Groundwork, Tally.
